Added the two uses of the name Lincoln Place, from the Mahlstedt fire survey plans (AI-assisted, Claude).

body.p: Lincoln Square appears on government plans as early as 1852. Given other local street names (e.g. Pelham Street) it seems probably that it is named after Henry Pelham-Clinton, 5th Duke of Newcastle and Earl of Lincoln who was Secretary of State for the Colonies in the early 1850s when Carlton was being laid out.
Lincoln Square is bounded to the east by Swanston Street, to the west by Bouverie Street, and Lincoln Place North and Lincoln Place South.

Which streets were called Lincoln Place changed over time. The MMBW plans of about 1895 name the sides of the square Lincoln Square North and South, while the directories list them as Lincoln Place. From 1900 the directories use Lincoln Place both for the square's sides and for a lane off Madeline Street, with the same house numbers. The Mahlstedt fire survey plans of 1923 to 1928 name the square's south side "Lincoln Square St." and give the name Lincoln Place to the lane running east from Bouverie Street to Swanston Street, south of Cumberland Place. The 1928 electoral roll fits this, with different people at Nos. 34 to 38 Lincoln Place and Nos. 34 to 38 Lincoln Square. The plans print no house numbers along the lane, so the Lincoln Place addresses of the 1920s can't yet be placed on it.
